stages.rough: Edit of the concept. Keep the small timber shelter with its shingled, patched roof on posts, the back wall with its small lattice window, the long plank table with stools, the tankards and the roast. Remove all three people. Remove the red rag on the roof. Beside a post lies a heavy log with two worn hand grips, and a stool is pushed back from the table as if someone just got up. Keep the same three-quarter isometric angle, ink outlines and warm light from the top left. No people anywhere. No letters, no runes, no loose cloth, no hard-edged ground slab, a feathered patch of natural ground on the same footprint, no painted cast shadows, no grey smoke or fog. Matte paint, no gloss.
stages.solid: The same hall one step on, painted between rough and grand. The shelter closes with plank walls on two sides and gains a first low dry-stone footing. The roof is a low, short, whole shingled roof, clearly smaller and lower than a grand hall's, with a plain ridge and no chimney, with simple crossed boards at each gable end. The long table is now seen through a wide open front with a covered bench. A lit doorway. The lifting log rests on two forked stands. A stiff wooden pennant on a pole. Keep the same three-quarter isometric angle, ink outlines and warm light from the top left. No people anywhere. No letters, no runes, no loose cloth, no hard-edged ground slab, a feathered patch of natural ground on the same footprint, no painted cast shadows, no grey smoke or fog. Matte paint, no gloss.
stages.grand: Edit of the concept. Keep the long timber mead hall, steep shingled roof, crossed carved beams at each gable, iron-banded posts, stone footing, the porch with benches, lit windows and warm doorway. Remove both men. Remove the grey smoke plume, keep only the roof vent. Through the door the long table can just be seen. Replace the torn feathered edge with a soft ground patch. Beside the steps, the lifting log and a pair of heavy stones on a timber rack. A clan banner stretched on a rigid wooden frame beside the porch. Keep the same three-quarter isometric angle, ink outlines and warm light from the top left. No people anywhere. No letters, no runes, no loose cloth, no hard-edged ground slab, a feathered patch of natural ground on the same footprint, no painted cast shadows, no grey smoke or fog. Matte paint, no gloss.
stages.mythic: Edit of the concept, going much further. Keep the dark stone walls, huge carved pillars, stone steps and open doors on firelight. Remove the fog. Remove all the banners and replace them with plain rigid carved panels bolted flat to the pillars, no symbols. The roof becomes a giant overturned longship: an immense black-oak hull of overlapping planks forming a tremendously high steep ridge, keel on top, and at each end its curved prow and sternpost sweep up and cross far above the gable, as high again as the hall, rising almost to the top of the canvas. The two stone hero statues on their plinths grow to twice the door height, at rest, each with both arms straight up holding one great round boulder over its head, no weapons. New magic: from the opening along the keel a steady ribbon of amber sparks climbs straight up between the crossed prows, and tall window slits blaze with the same unnatural amber fire, readable by day, no smoke. A plain carved shield with amber light in its surface over the doors, no symbol. The first plank table and stool stand small on the top step. Unmistakably a building, no floating. Keep the same three-quarter isometric angle, ink outlines and warm light from the top left. No people anywhere. No letters, no runes, no loose cloth, no hard-edged ground slab, a feathered patch of natural ground on the same footprint, no painted cast shadows, no grey smoke or fog. Matte paint, no gloss.
